item.title: Version 1.0.9
item.description:
• New: a warning when a full tunnel lets IPv4 or IPv6 traffic out over the physical network, with a "Disable IPv6" button in the menu bar
  • Fix: a routing loop could send the tunnel's own packets back into it right after connecting; the endpoint route is now set first and a firewall rule drops looped packets
  • Security: peer preshared keys are no longer sent to the app by the privileged helper
  • Security: the privileged helper no longer allows unsigned libraries
  • Security: users can no longer remove each other's split-tunnel and multi-hop routes
  • Fix: the WireGuard tools list in Settings for builds made with Homebrew coreutils

Notes

  • Existing installs will be prompted to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading
  • The firewall (pf) is now enabled for every tunnel that manages routes, not only with the kill switch

item.title: Version 1.0.8
item.description:
• Security: the privileged helper now installs the WireGuard tools itself, only from the signed app, and checks them before every use; modified tools are replaced and logged
  • Security: the privileged helper checks the app's signature on every request, so another program can no longer impersonate WireTunnels
  • Security: the helper now enforces shared-tunnel permissions and tunnel ownership itself, so a standard user can no longer stop, replace or change tunnels they are not allowed to
  • No more Install Tools step: approving the helper is enough
  • New: On-Demand Ethernet rules can be limited to subnets, to connect at the office but not at home
  • Network changes are handled one at a time and tunnels the rules forbid are no longer restarted after wake; tunnel toggles are disabled while connecting
  • Quit works even if the helper was removed while the app was running

Notes

  • Existing installs will be prompted to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading

item.title: Version 1.0.7
item.description:
• Kill switch fixed: it now really blocks traffic outside the tunnel while it is enabled
  • Security: closed wg-quick hook filter bypasses that could run commands as root from a crafted configuration
  • New: per-tunnel inventory command that adds discovered IPs/CIDRs to a tunnel's AllowedIPs and routes, and keeps them protected outside the VPN
  • New: Search Domains field for tunnels, applied while connected and restored on disconnect
  • New: duplicate a tunnel, monochrome menu bar icon and an automatic update-check setting
  • Automatic reconnect failures no longer pop up alerts: the menu bar shows connecting, reconnecting or connection lost, with Retry and Details
  • Quitting waits for tunnels to disconnect and DNS to be restored, and lets you retry or cancel if cleanup fails
  • DNS only changes on the active network and is repaired after an interrupted setup
  • Fixed the error shown after waking from sleep and an empty editor for shared tunnels
  • The menu closes when you click elsewhere, tunnel names are preserved and saved metadata is protected from corruption

Notes

  • Existing installs will be prompted to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading
  • If you use the kill switch, traffic is now blocked whenever its tunnel is down; turn it off per tunnel if you do not want that
  • If your DNS still points to a VPN-only server from an older version, reset it in System Settings > Network > Details > DNS

item.title: Version 1.0.6
item.description:
• Split DNS: send only chosen domains (for example lan or corp.example) to a tunnel's DNS servers while everything else keeps using your normal DNS. Set it per tunnel, including shared tunnels (administrators)
  • Tunnel names up to 50 characters now work everywhere: importing, creating and editing a profile no longer fails on names longer than 15 characters, and the name you chose is the one you see
  • Fixed two client profiles for the same server (same server key and port) both showing as connected when only one was actually running, and the "Invalid or missing tunnel configuration" error when turning the other one off
  • Shared tunnels: administrators can now allow or block other users from connecting and/or disconnecting a shared tunnel, from the tunnel's own detail page
  • New "Start in Background" setting: skip opening the dashboard window on launch (pairs well with "Hide Dock Icon" for a menu-bar-only app)
  • New administrator option to require an admin password to turn off "Launch at Login"

Notes

  • Existing installs will be prompted to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading
  • If you turn Split DNS on or off for a connected tunnel, you'll be asked whether to reconnect it, since that is when the system-wide DNS is decided
  • WireTunnels only manages the resolver files it created for Split DNS; existing resolver configuration for the same domain is left untouched
  • The administrator Launch-at-Login option only governs WireTunnels' own Settings — it doesn't prevent disabling the login item from System Settings directly

item.title: Version 1.0.5
item.description:
• Tunnels now automatically reconnect when a peer's dynamic-DNS/IP address changes, instead of going silently dead
  • Fixed an active tunnel not reconnecting after your Mac's local IP renewed via DHCP
  • Fixed tunnels not reliably reconnecting or auto-connecting/disconnecting after your Mac wakes from sleep
  • Fixed Allowed IPs occasionally getting mixed up between tunnels after reconnecting
  • Fixed two tunnels sharing the same server but different ports being incorrectly treated as connected/overlapping together
  • Fixed the kill switch toggle silently re-arming itself every time you opened a tunnel's details
  • Fixed several multi-hop issues: reconnecting a lone chain member after disconnecting the chain, On-Demand rules disconnecting an individually-connected chain member, stale DNS left behind after disconnecting a chain, and a lost route after sleep/wake
  • Multi-hop: a chain member's own On-Demand rule no longer brings up or tears down the whole chain — only that tunnel
  • Fixed tunnel names being silently truncated to 15 characters — now up to 50
  • Administrators can now edit a shared tunnel's name and config directly, not just replace the whole file

Notes

  • Existing installs will be prompted to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading
  • Multi-hop chains still connect and disconnect as a unit only from the Multi-Hop screen

item.title: Version 1.0
item.description:
• Initial release of WireTunnels
  • Manage WireGuard tunnels from the menu bar and dashboard
  • Privileged helper for secure tunnel management
  • Import, create, and edit tunnel configurations
  • Auto-connect on network changes

item.title: Version 1.0.1
item.description: • Fixed privileged helper detection: the app could report the helper as "not installed" or stuck requiring approval even when it was actually enabled, because status was read from a long-lived cached handle instead of a fresh system query

item.title: Version 1.0.2
item.description:
• Shared tunnels: administrators can create tunnels visible to every user on the Mac, control who's allowed to connect or disconnect, and see who's currently connected
  • On-Demand rules can now connect and disconnect on different Wi-Fi networks independently, instead of a single action per tunnel
  • Pick Wi-Fi networks for On-Demand rules from a list of known networks, or type one manually
  • Shared tunnel changes now ask for your admin password once per session instead of every time
  • Added a "Hide Dock Icon" option in Settings for menu-bar-only use
  • Fixed On-Demand rules for specific Wi-Fi networks not triggering (this needed Location permission to read the current network name)

item.title: Version 1.0.3
item.description:
• Reliable reconnect after sleep — tunnels now automatically restart after your Mac wakes, instead of the dashboard silently showing "Connected" while traffic has actually stopped
  • Per-tunnel kill switch — block all other network traffic if a tunnel drops unexpectedly, until it reconnects or you turn it off; works for personal tunnels and for shared tunnels (administrator-controlled)
  • QR code import/export — show a tunnel as a QR code to pair a phone with the official WireGuard app in seconds, or import a tunnel by dropping, opening, or pasting a QR code image
  • Live throughput sparkline + connection test — each tunnel row now shows a live throughput sparkline, and the tunnel detail view has an on-demand "Test Connection" button that checks latency to your VPN server

Notes

  • The kill switch enforces its rules via the system packet filter (PF) through the existing privileged helper — no new permissions beyond what's already required
  • The connection test only pings the tunnel's own configured VPN server; it makes no calls to any third-party service, consistent with WireTunnels' no-telemetry design
  • Existing installs will prompt to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading (required for the kill switch's new helper capability)

item.title: Version 1.0.4
item.description:
• Fixed tunnels not reliably reconnecting or auto-connecting/disconnecting after your Mac wakes from sleep
  • Fixed Allowed IPs occasionally getting mixed up between tunnels after reconnecting
  • Tunnel speed test: optionally set your own URL per tunnel to measure throughput alongside the existing latency check
  • Shortcuts support: connect, disconnect, disconnect all, or check which tunnels are connected — from Shortcuts, Siri, or Raycast
  • Split tunnel exclusions: exclude specific IP ranges from a tunnel at runtime, without editing the config or reconnecting
  • Multi-hop: chain two tunnels together so traffic exits through a second server, hiding your real IP from the exit server

Notes

  • The speed test only runs against a URL you set yourself — there is no built-in default host
  • Split tunnel exclusions and multi-hop use the same privileged helper mechanism as the existing kill switch — no new permissions beyond what's already required
  • Existing installs will be prompted to update the privileged helper on first launch after upgrading (required for the new routing capability)
  • Multi-hop chains connect and disconnect as a unit only from the Multi-Hop screen — each tunnel's own On-Demand rule still connects/disconnects just that tunnel, not the chain
  • Only the exit tunnel in a multi-hop chain manages your DNS server, so it's correctly restored to your real network's DNS once you disconnect
